memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come here and listen to the words of the Lord your God. This is how you will know that the living God is among you and that he will certainly drive out before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites and Jebusites. See, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth will go into the Jordan ahead of you." — Josh 3:9-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua gathers the people and gives them a title for God that should make our hearts leap: "the living God." Not a carved idol that cannot move or speak, not a distant force, but the living God who acts, who keeps His word, who is present among His people. The Canaanite nations trusted in lifeless idols; Israel followed a God who was alive and active.

And this living God is also "the Lord of all the earth." He is not merely a local, tribal deity powerful only in one region. He owns and rules the whole earth, including the land of the Canaanites and every enemy standing in the way. When the Lord of all the earth goes ahead of you, no obstacle can finally stand.

Joshua points to the ark going into the Jordan as the proof: "This is how you will know that the living God is among you." God was about to demonstrate His living presence in a way no one could deny.

For us, the living God has come near in Jesus, who is "the resurrection and the life" (John 11:25) and who conquered the grave. We do not serve a dead teacher or a distant idea; we follow a risen, living Lord who is with us always. The same living God who parted the Jordan is present in our lives today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you truly live as though God is the living God, active and present?
2. What "idols" — lifeless things you trust — compete with the living God in your heart?
3. How does knowing God is "Lord of all the earth" shape the way you face obstacles?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Living God, Lord of all the earth, thank You that You are present and active among Your people. Help me trust You above every lifeless thing I am tempted to lean on. Amen.
